title: No framing traps in history content
statement: History and technology content avoids known framing traps, such as monolithic groups, events as destiny, contested readings as settled fact, one side without agency, lone-genius invention and unexamined sources.
detail: A Grade 4 reading course's generation contract makes misconception screening a gate on generation and runs its history and social-studies texts through checks for settled-fact framing of contested interpretation, inevitability and monolithic groups. A Grade 6 course's misconception check bans, in passages on design and invention, invention as a lone flash of genius, a design as perfect or finished, and technology as inevitable progress. A Grade 3 unit on Native nations names treating them as one group, or as a people who exist only in the past, as the misconception to guard against, and requires its content to be checked for nation names, present-tense framing and respectful, accurate traditions. The first trap is also part of keeping fact and interpretation apart.
against: The unit review is marked historical and superseded as a review request, though nothing withdraws its controls (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz::apush/docs/UNIT-1-REVIEW.md`, line 5).

evidence.quote: (no settled-fact framing of contested interpretation; no inevitability; no monolithic groups)
invention as a lone flash of genius; a design as "perfect"/finished; technology as inevitable progress.
Native nations are **many distinct, present-day peoples** — not one single group, and not a people who exist only in the past.
verify nation names, present-tense framing, and that traditions are represented respectfully and accurately.
5. **Representation gate:** A group is not treated as internally uniform when the lesson's own scope depends on regional, political, class, racial, gender, religious, or strategic differences.

The unit explicitly checks recurring high-risk simplifications: - treating Indigenous societies as one culture; - turning environmental constraint into destiny; - reducing exploration to motives without capabilities; - presenting the Columbian Exchange as a balanced list; - treating encomienda as land ownership or all coerced labor as identical; - presenting caste categories as a perfectly rigid universal hierarchy; - explaining conquest as a single European action without Indigenous diplomacy, alliance, or resistance; - treating a source as transparent narration or dismissing it with an unsupported "bias" label.
Inevitability framing ("the colonies were always going to become America") — history as choices under uncertainty, not destiny.
Monolithic groups ("the colonists thought… the Native peoples believed…") → specific peoples, specific colonies, specific voices.
The paired colonist-vs-Native accounts are the guard: two positioned sources, neither presented as the neutral truth.
